data.body:
DECISION UNDER THE RESCOPED CRITERIA — S6 PASSES. Superseding the "do not claim first-class"
recommendation in my earlier decision comment, which was written against the pre-rescope ACs.

WHAT CHANGED. The operator ruled that LLM non-determinism is expected and that comparing two
MODELS' judgements against each other is out of epic 061c's scope. The epic's scope is that the
same PAYLOADS reach the LLM and the same TOOLS are available, regardless of model and provider.
0d76's ACs were retargeted accordingly. My earlier judgement — that the ticket could not honestly
close as "Bedrock cleared the bar" — was correct under the OLD criteria; the criteria were the
problem, not the measurement.

RECLASSIFICATION, so the record is unambiguous. The paired-run ParityReport recorded earlier on
this ticket is now INFORMATIONAL EVIDENCE, not a gate:
  * standard 1 decision flip, frontier 2 flips, frontier verdict agreement 0.929
  * frontier false-accept "rose 0.143"
These compare two DIFFERENT MODELS' judgements and are therefore out of scope. They are NOT S6
failures and do NOT trigger the remediate-or-drop criterion. (The false-accept item is separately
moot: 62ac has since landed and corrected that metric's inversion, and re-scoring the recorded
run offline turned v1 0.786 -> v2 0.929 "rose" into v1 0.214 -> v2 0.071, a 14.3pp IMPROVEMENT.)

WHAT S6 ACTUALLY GATES, and its status — ALL PASS:
  1. PAYLOAD PARITY .......... PASS. Captured outbound requests, both class slots, with and
     without a requested temperature: system prompt, messages, max_tokens and temperature all
     equivalent; the model id is the ONLY differing field. Envelope differences enumerated (8 of
     them). Evidence in the preceding comment.
  2. TOOL PARITY ............. PASS. 6 tools, identical names, descriptions and input schemas on
     both providers, both slots.
  3. CAPABILITY DIFFERENCES .. PASS, one found and explicit: `temperature` is withdrawn from
     opus on BOTH providers and sent to sonnet on BOTH, driven by the model's
     `supports_temperature: False` capability record rather than by the provider. Nothing else
     altered either payload.
  4. PROVIDER-CLEAN ROUTING .. PASS. Zero non-Bedrock calls across 84/84 v2 case-runs on each of
     the two slots.
  5. BEDROCK INVOKABILITY .... PASS. Both inference-profile ids invoke in 896586841071/us-east-1;
     neither slot is unmeasured, so the unmeasured-slot criterion does not apply.

REMEDIATION REQUIRED: NONE. No payload difference, no tool difference, no undocumented
capability difference, and no provider-routing leak was found. Bedrock's first-class claim is
supported by the evidence this story was retargeted to produce.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE STILL TRUE AND SHOULD TRAVEL TO S8 (eb6e), neither a blocker:
  * Bedrock's `cachePoint` marker carries NO TTL, where Anthropic's `cache_control` carries
    `ttl: "5m"`. rebar sets no non-default TTL today, so this is latent — but it is a real
    expressiveness difference, not merely different spelling, and it would bite if a non-default
    TTL is ever introduced.
  * Cost/throughput shape, measured: the standard slot ran 9.9% FASTER on Bedrock and the
    frontier slot within 0.1%, which retires the N=1 pilot's "~35% slower" hint. Per-case-run
    cost is far higher than the plan assumed (the code-review arm is agentic, ~100k input tokens
    and ~8.6 provider requests per case-run), which S8 should cost the cutover against.
